title: Lifting the tempo for tired bandsmen and being Duke's lieutenant
summary: Greer slept on a cot with coffee royal and lifted tempo; Duke yawned at the piano; Greer was his right-hand man.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Only thing, if the band -- like we were playing this theater with the band, we had the first show, say about 11:30. A lot of times them cats would stay out so late they're scared to go home. They come to the theater and go to sleep. Now, when they come downstairs Duke could tell, they're going to get a little sluggish, see. I stayed out with them but I had the theater; a valet when I get to/had the coffee and a little taste--coffee Royal, I had eight hours sleep by the first show and I ain't saw no bed. And them guys, at the first note I would take it up a little, just a little, not a whole lot, just a little to give them that inspiration. Duke knew it, none of the other guys -- say, "How did he start like us and don't feel tired like us?" I'd say, "Man, I had eight hours sleep before I come down here." I'd say, "Jonesy is my valet. He had that café royale for me. I'm wide awake."

Of course, after the first show, I've got to hit that cot, too, you know. I never let them get a chance to overtake me, tiredness overtake me. That's when Duke -- have you ever seen Duke play with his back to the audience?
Man, Duke used to stand up, they thought that was so cute, he'd stand up playing the piano and looking up at me and yawning. I'd say, "Come on here, daddy, let's go."
I had to keep hollering at him, talking to him, you know, keep him awake. Soon as we'd come off stage, he'd fall off and faint on the thing, man.
So in a certain way, as far as keeping the band going, you were more or less Ellington's right-hand man with the band? Musically and otherwise.
Yeah, I was. I was like a lieutenant to him. He could depend on me. All the way through, he could depend on me, all the way through.
